analysis: The trial executed successfully but achieved macro validation HR@10=0.3700, below the preceding ItemAttention result of 0.3825 by 0.0125 and the reported SASRec baseline of 0.505 by 0.135. Category HR@10 was 0.405 for Movies_and_TV, 0.360 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.295 for Electronics, and 0.420 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Adding contextual history encoding did not improve the aggregate result under the retained training protocol. This weakens the hypothesis that missing sequence context was the main limitation; the results do not establish whether optimization, positional encoding, or candidate-conditioned pooling caused the decline. No held-out test conclusions are available.
code_summary: One independently trained ItemAttention network and one selected checkpoint per category. History embeddings receive learned positions and two causal Transformer blocks with width 96, two heads, and dropout 0.2. Normalized contextual representations feed candidate-conditioned attention and value pooling; normalized target compatibility uses learned scales, recency decay, and jointly trained item biases. Padding masks prevent fully masked attention rows and zero padded outputs. Training retains prefix sampling, 127 uniform negatives, cross-entropy, embedding regularization, and AdamW. Checkpoints record architecture configuration; the generated routed predictor reconstructs each network and strictly loads its selected state dictionary.
